The dominant allele does not prevent the recessive one from entering a gamete. Therefore, half the gametes receive the purple allele, and half receive the white allele. So the correct probability is actually 50%. This distinction is crucial for predicting inheritance patterns later. Only the pp genotype expresses the white trait. This means three out of four offspring will be purple, and only one will be white.
